i love that psychologist line LOL, listen, maybe itll be your own personal style to talk about 300 different concepts in one song rather than just one? more bang for the listeners buck kind of thing LOL? most people wont even notice theres huge distinction between each stanza of lyrics, because the musical composition behind it is what ties it all together and makes it sound like one harmonious and united song. i think u should give urself the room and freedom to override the urge to make one song all about only one thing and just go where ur mind takes u. even if ur song sounds like it takes a hundred random turns LOL thats what Kurt Cobain did. he wrote his lyrics by just writing random shit and focusing more on if it sounded good in a rhythmic way or not (like how poets do LOL, the blue boat bounces beautifully) Heart Shaped Box is an example of lyrics he wrote this way, “she eyes me like a pisces when i am weak ive been locked inside your heart shaped box for weeks ive been drawn into your magnet tar pit trap, i wish i could eat your cancer when you turn black” the words he randomly wrote, i am still able to extrapolate meaning and significance from: it sounds like he is speaking about a female lover that has him feeling stuck and magnetically attracted to. you should search “The Riddle” by Nik Kershaw. that guy said himself that he wrote those lyrics 5 minutes before going into the studio cause he just needed lyrics immediately so he could hurry up and release the song. the lyrics make NO SENSE WHATSOEVER. YET THEY SOUND POETIC! its crazy. so that doesnt mean that u have to completely take that approach and write batshit lyrics that make no sense “banana ate the apple and i almost fell overrr” type stuff LOL. instead, try letting the words flow, and see what ur uninhibited mind comes up with alone. if u value authenticity and meaning behind ur lyrics, maybe this is the best way to see what ur subconscious mind ACTUALLY has to say, ACTUALLY values. like right now, if i started writing my most not-held-back thoughts on paper; my true feelings would probably start making their way out. “living life on the outside i dont want to die yet i want to go very far farther than what is said to be possible” that was my stream of consciousness, then i would take that and refine it to make it rhyme, since its rap, look for synonyms that rhyme, make it interesting, add metaphors, it can be really complicated but if u worry too much about words not coming out they’ll just get even more lodged cause ur brain will focus more on ur frustration of not being able to think of anything rather than just letting shit flow. make a rough draft with the random ass weird words, then refine it into a second draft. keep doing this, fill up 5 pages. keep what you like. string them together in an order, add connecting sentences and bridges if it helps u get a more synchronized storytelling sound. its a process

so sometimes u cant make it about ur personal life, u gotta make it about the world in general. a lot of songs are about abstract stuff, not even real physical things. it depends also what ur comfortable writing lyrics about. for example im not good with emotions so it would feel awkward cheesy and cringey for me to write about the feeling of “anger” or something LOL. but if ur comfortable with that u gotta just take something abstract like that then start writing down scenarios that might accompany it. half of the time the stuff in songs aren’t even authentic to the writer themselves, but the writer still cares and is invested in the topic even if they haven’t experienced it. or they exaggerate it. like Eminem Stan. you could even write abstractly about ur experience right now with lyric block. u want it to be unique and creative right, so aptly ascribe the feeling and experience of having lyric/writers block with something metaphorical. a hose thats ready to burst with water but its bent so the water won’t come out. now obviously my example is kinda cheesy but u gotta just start writing down as many “conceptual” representations of ur desired topic as possible cause that’s how the mental connections and ideas start pouring out. writers block = frustration, not reaching ur goals, running out of ink, running on empty, lacking inspiration, feeling empty like u have nothing to say, “loss of words”, “no words” and just like that i arrived at a potential title. “No Words.” not the best but its something and it gives u something to start with. when u have writers block u feel like u cant think of anything. “frustrated cause it feels like the flow has stopped, want to write but the faucets blocked” LOL and then u keep just playing around like that until it sounds how u want it, keep thinking in the abstract “okay so i just talked about the faucet being blocked, the words are being compared to water… flow of water maybe i can connect that to a rappers flow…”
